capability.summary: Extract CREATE TABLE names, columns, types, and constraint-class names from SQL DDL
capability.description: Parses one UTF-8 SQL file with sqlglot's default dialect, keeps CREATE TABLE statements, and returns a custom tables/columns JSON summary. Despite its name, it does not emit a standards-compliant JSON Schema document.
capability.problem_space: Coarse structural extraction from CREATE TABLE DDL into a custom JSON table summary; not JSON Schema generation, SQL execution, database introspection, dialect-specific validation, constraint semantics, or round-trip DDL conversion.

constraint.io_signature: Input: required file_path string naming an existing UTF-8 SQL DDL file. Output: JSON envelope with tables [{table, columns:[{name,type,constraints}]}] or a handled sqlglot ParseError; no database is contacted.
accepted_inputs: an existing UTF-8 SQL text file containing statements parseable by sqlglot's default dialect
constraint.output_shape: Success: {status: "success", tool: "sqlglot", target: string, tables: [{table: string|null, columns: [{name: string, type: string|null, constraints: [string]}]}]}, exit 0; valid SQL with no recognized CREATE TABLE yields tables=[]. Missing path: {status: "error", message: string}, exit 2. Caught ParseError: {status: "error", tool: "sqlglot", message: string}, exit 1. Missing argument prints usage to stderr and exits 1 without JSON; file I/O and non-ParseError failures may traceback.
limitations: output is a custom table summary and is not JSON Schema: it has no `$schema`, object properties, required arrays, validation keywords, references, or SQL-to-JSON type mapping
accepts one existing UTF-8 SQL file; a directory or a multi-file DDL project target is outside this wrapper's input boundary
uses sqlglot's default dialect with no caller-selectable dialect and ignores non-CREATE-TABLE statements
constraint output contains sqlglot constraint class names rather than complete SQL expressions or semantics, and table-name extraction may not cover every CREATE form
reads the complete SQL input with no timeout or input-size limit; the generated custom tables/columns summary has no output truncation, so large inputs or large results can amplify memory use
does not execute SQL, contact a database, or modify the input

output_contract.description: JSON envelope containing a custom CREATE TABLE/column summary; it is not a standards-compliant JSON Schema.

json_schema.description: Native JSON representation only; no field or task-delivery guarantee.

intent_tags: extract table and column metadata from SQL DDL
summarize CREATE TABLE statements as custom JSON
negative_intents: execute SQL or inspect a live database
validate SQL for a selected database dialect
